scope: D099 universal-form depiction; visual contract, not art approval.
identity: Vishnu as the single universal person described in D099 stanzas 8–9.
anatomy: One connected central cosmic body. The verse’s plural heads, eyes and feet are represented as orderly symbolic tiers of many distinct, attached features, not duplicated full bodies or random extra limbs. Keep one central face and coherent torso.
palette: Deep matte blue central form against mineral cream, ochre and muted cosmic fields; dark drawn contours, shallow mural space.
iconography: A heart-lotus may symbolize the indwelling presence; three restrained world bands may symbolize the lower triad. No weapons unless the scene plan calls for them.
never: no rays, beams, text or gloss
no replacement of the source’s universal form with a second physical Vishnu

depiction_rules.notes: This is an explicitly cosmic multiform depiction, distinct from ordinary two-armed Guruvayurappan murti anatomy. Represent plurality as ordered mural symbolism.
